svg.text: RTL X-Optimism vs. Gate-Level X-Pessimism on Identical Logic
Why RTL Simulation Masks Uninitialized Control Bugs While Synthesized Gate Netlists Propagate Unknown 'X's
1. RTL Behavioral X-Optimism (False Pass!)
// Suppose uninitialized `sel = 1'bx` at boot!
always_comb begin
if (sel) out = a; // sel == 1'bx evaluates FALSE!
else out = b; // RTL picks `else` silently!
end
Verilog `if (x)` ignores true branch & executes `else` branch!
Same Hazard in `case (state)` Without `default: 'x`:
RTL hides un-reset `sel` or corrupt `case` indices cleanly, giving
verification teams false confidence before synthesis.
Early Cure: Turn on VCS `-xprop=tmerge` or Xcelium `-xprop` in RTL
regressions BEFORE even waiting for GLS netlists!
2. Gate-Level Boolean X-Pessimism (False Fail!)
// Suppose A = 1, B = 1, and S = 1'bx (both data = 1!):
Synthesized 2:1 MUX = (A & ~S) | (B & S);
1. Gate 1: (1 & ~x) = x | Gate 2: (1 & x) = x
2. OR Gate: (x | x) = 1'bx <-- FALSE 'X' IN SILICON!
In real CMOS, whether S resolves 0 or 1, output is ALWAYS 1!
Boolean AOI22 gates lose correlation (`~S` vs `S` cancellation).
Foundry Fix: X-Aware MUX UDP Truth Tables
// A B S : Y (Matched in foundry MX2 cell UDP!)
1 1 ? : 1; // Passes 1 even when S == 1'bx!
0 0 ? : 0; // Passes 0 even when S == 1'bx!
And for custom RTL-like flops (`D ^ ~D`), keep muxes in UDP!
